text:
Alexander Wennberg has one goal this season, and it took until November 23 to come. The chances were never the problem. He has generated 4.34 expected goals in 16 games, his shooting percentage sits at 3.7%, and our talent range puts his true finishing somewhere between 11% and 16%. This is the textbook case of a player who is due.

The 16 games tell the other part of the story. His log has a gap from October 19 to November 9, and San Jose Hockey Now has written about him playing through injury since he returned. He's still logging close to 20 minutes a night, and Sharks Hockey Digest's Max Miller has been raving about his line with Misa and Toffoli.

Wennberg has never been a scorer first. Evolving-Hockey had his value last season coming almost entirely from defense, with opponents getting fewer chances when he was out there and his offensive impact in the bottom 2% of forwards. On a team built around Macklin Celebrini, his job is to take the hard minutes. Watch the faceoff circle: Miller noted he took a draw for the first time since returning only after Celebrini was waved out.
